**A Detailed History of Mount Gretna, Pennsylvania**

Mount Gretna, a borough in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, is defined by a unique convergence of 19th-century industrial development, military training, and the Victorian-era Chautauqua movement. Its history is less about typical commercial growth and more about its intentional development as a cultural and recreational retreat.

**Founding and Subdivisions**
The roots of Mount Gretna trace back to **1883**, when local iron magnate Robert Coleman sought a picnic grove along his **Cornwall and Lebanon Railroad (C&LRR)**, establishing the area [https://mtgretnahistory.org/]. The site was initially a wilderness until the railroad brought it onto the map [https://lebtown.com/2025/07/02/how-mount-gretna-went-from-a-howling-wilderness-to-a-paradise-for-visitors/]. While it is a formally recognized borough, historical sources focus more on its institutional identity (the Chautauqua) than on specific modern neighborhood subdivisions.

**Military History**
Mount Gretna’s early history was profoundly influenced by military use. In **1885**, the Pennsylvania National Guard began a 50-year annual encampment at Mt. Gretna. This made it the state’s first dedicated permanent training area. This military function continued until the establishment of Fort Indiantown Gap in the 1930s [https://mtgretna.com/about-gretna/our-history/].

**Cultural and Religious History (The Chautauqua Movement)**
Mount Gretna's defining characteristic is its embodiment of the **Chautauqua movement**, a Victorian-era phenomenon that combined religious instruction, education, and recreation [https://www.inquirer.com/news/pennsylvania/mount-gretna-lebanon-county-pennsylvania-chautauqua-paradise-20230820.html].

*   **Origin:** The movement was inspired by the original Chautauqua Institution, established in New York State in **1874** [https://explorepahistory.com/hmarker.php%3FmarkerId=1-A-37A.html].
*   **Local Founding:** The Pennsylvania Chautauqua officially began in **1892** when a group of **Evangelical United Brethren** members decided the area would serve as a center for these activities [https://lebtown.com/2025/06/03/pennsylvanias-133-year-old-chautauqua-brings-the-movements-four-pillars/].
*   **Pillars:** The Mount Gretna Chautauqua operates on the four foundational pillars: **Arts, Education, Religion, and Recreation** [https://lancastercountymag.com/mount-gretna-historically-steeped-in-the-arts-education/].

**Summer Recreation Site and Attractions**
Mount Gretna is widely regarded as the **"Pennsylvania Chautauqua"** and functions as a dedicated summer recreation site. Its attractions have developed alongside the Chautauqua tradition:

*   **Tour of Homes and Gardens:** Established in **1892**, this attraction manifested the social and cultural phenomenon of the era [https://pahistoricpreservation.com/offbeat-outing-mt-gretna-tour-of-homes-and-gardens/].
*   **Arts Focus:** The town is deeply steeped in the arts, hosting a well-known outdoor art show in August, which draws international visitors for two days [https://lancastercountymag.com/mount-gretna-historically-steeped-in-the-arts-education/]. Throughout the year, the town features concerts and festivals [https://visitlebanonvalley.com/mt-gretna/].

**Businesses Since Founding**
Specific long-standing commercial businesses are primarily institutional, tied to the Chautauqua movement and the early railroad development:

*   **Cornwall and Lebanon Railroad (C&LRR):** Established in **1883** by Robert Coleman, this railroad was the initial economic catalyst for the town [https://mtgretnahistory.org/].
*   **Chautauqua Institutions:** The **Pennsylvania Chautauqua** (starting 1892) and the **Tour of Homes and Gardens** (starting 1892) represent the foundational, continuous institutional presence in Mount Gretna.

***

**Summary of Evidence:**

*   **Founding:** 1883, by Robert Coleman, linked to the C&LRR [https://mtgretnahistory.org/].
*   **Military:** 1885, 50+ years of Pennsylvania National Guard encampment [https://mtgretna.com/about-gretna/our-history/].
*   **Culture/Religion:** 1892, establishment of the Pennsylvania Chautauqua by Evangelical United Brethren members, based on the 1874 NY model [https://lebtown.com/2025/06/03/pennsylvanias-133-year-old-chautauqua-brings-the-movements-four-pillars/].
*   **Attractions/Subdivisions:** Tour of Homes and Gardens (1892); no specific formal subdivisions detailed; recognized as a recreational/cultural destination [https://pahistoricpreservation.com/offbeat-outing-mt-gretna-tour-of-homes-and-gardens/].
*   **Businesses:** C&LRR (1883), Chautauqua Institution (1892), Tour of Homes and Gardens (1892) [https://mtgretnahistory.org/].
